clue.text: Mediterranean resort not in favour of taking most of the elite

parts.note: anti means against, not in favour of

indicators.note: most of says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the best means the elite, the top people

explanation.surface: A holiday town on the Med that disapproves of hosting the cream of society.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibes is a well-known resort town on the French Riviera coast.

clue.text: Open hostility in publicity for Tony, Oscar etc

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: ads, advertisements, are publicity
open hostility between nations is war

explanation.surface: Showbiz feuds played out in the press around the Tonys and Oscars.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonys and Oscars are examples of prizes handed out in theatre and film.

clue.text: Ruler in Volunteer State is emperor

indicators.note: in places the ruler inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: Tennessee is nicknamed the Volunteer State; its postal abbreviation is TN
a raja is an Indian ruler or prince

explanation.surface: A ruler in Tennessee turns out to be an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volunteer' looks like a soldier, but the Volunteer State is the US nickname for Tennessee.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan was a Roman emperor of the second century AD.

clue.text: Stubborn fish with bleeding heart

parts.note: the bullhead is a small freshwater fish

indicators.note: heart of a word means its middle letters, here of bleeding

explanation.surface: A fish is pictured with a bleeding heart, perhaps hooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullheaded is an idiom for obstinate, pushing ahead like a bull.

clue.text: Jolly good little police officer

definitions.meaning: a dated exclamation of approval, jolly good
the short form of superintendent, a senior police rank

explanation.surface: Praise for a junior constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is both a hearty word of approval and a clipped superintendent.

clue.text: Theatre with a bit of lino — enthusiasts may wax it

parts.note: the Lyric is a London theatre name, used for many theatres

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A theatre floor covered in lino that keen people polish with wax.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has fans waxing a floor; the definition rests on the idiom 'wax lyrical', to speak gushingly. The Lyric is a West End theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax lyrical is to enthuse, so enthusiasts may wax this adjective.

clue.text: Latin composition for Keats, Poe, Wordsworth, Southey and Coleridge

indicators.note: composition means putting letters together afresh, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Writing in Latin by a list of famous English-language poets.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats and Poe look like part of the list of poets, but they are anagram fodder; only the last three names define.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth, Southey and Coleridge lived in the Lake District and were grouped as this school.

clue.text: We hear whisky's to go up

indicators.note: we hear says the word is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: rye is a whisky, and whisky's read as ryes

explanation.surface: A claim that whisky prices are set to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise is to go up, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Attlee given a pair of tights before introduction to social climber

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the last one

parts.note: Clement Attlee, post-war British Prime Minister, was known as Clem

indicators.note: a pair of here takes the first two letters of tights
the introduction to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Clement Attlee, kitted out in tights, being presented to an ambitious social upstart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social climber' looks like one phrase, but the climber is the plant; 'pair of' gives TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing plant, so a climber in the gardening sense.

clue.text: Portrait I know not so much about

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other

parts.note: less means not so much
ken is Scots for to know

explanation.surface: A painter admitting they are not much good at portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: A likeness is a picture or representation of a person, a portrait.

clue.text: Advantage of a disguise for the auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so this is about the words heard

parts.note: a veil is a disguise for the face

explanation.surface: An accountant benefits from wearing a mask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant; here it means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail is benefit or advantage, as in 'to no avail'.

clue.text: Fish, say, in a Colorado resort

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
to say is to speak

explanation.surface: A fish turns up, for example, at a holiday spot in Colorado.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example'; it is a verb giving SPEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Pikes Peak is a Colorado mountain popular with tourists.

clue.text: Dangerous things that spread destruction

indicators.note: destruction of the words breaks them up so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of hazards that cause widespread ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Death traps are structures or places so unsafe they could kill.

clue.text: Pop, pop (two ways)

parts.note: pop is father, pa
two compass directions, W for west and N for north

explanation.surface: A word repeated, with a hint that it has two meanings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two ways' seems to say pop has two senses; it gives two compass points. The second pop is slang for pledging goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop something is to hock it, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Affectionate feeling shown by nurses cradling birds

indicators.note: cradling means holding within, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
ernes are sea eagles

explanation.surface: Nurses holding baby birds show warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness is gentle affection, a feeling of fond care.

clue.text: Chimera seen to reconcile bitter foes?

indicators.note: to reconcile is to rearrange into agreement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A mythical monster is seen bringing sworn enemies together.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the irony: reconciling arch-enemies is unlikely.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch-enemies are chief adversaries, the bitterest foes.

clue.text: One constellation or another discovered after intergalactic space mission ends

indicators.note: discovered after says the following piece comes later
ends of the three words means their last letters

parts.note: another constellation here is Taurus, the Bull

explanation.surface: Astronomers spot a new star group after a space mission winds up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One constellation or another' reads as a single vague phrase; it splits into the definition and TAURUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaurus is a large southern constellation, the Centaur.

clue.text: Flower seen on top of mountain by an agricultural worker

parts.note: stock is a garden flower

indicators.note: top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A flower spotted high on a mountain by a farmhand.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockman tends farm animals, an agricultural worker.

clue.text: Excited by a small bet

parts.note: a flutter is British slang for a small wager

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at placing a modest wager.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is everyday British for a modest bet, as on a horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflutter means nervously excited, heart fluttering.

clue.text: A sweet odour many found pretentious

parts.note: toffee is a sweet
nose is the smell of a wine, its odour
D is 500 in Roman numerals, read as many

explanation.surface: Many people judge a sugary smell to be affected.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee-nosed is British slang for snobbish, stuck-up.

clue.text: Unvarying? Very!

definitions.meaning: ever means always, and so means in the same way, so together they suggest constancy

explanation.surface: A query answered with an emphatic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever so is a colloquial intensifier meaning extremely.

clue.text: A suspension involving right or wrong

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a stay is a suspension, as a stay of execution

explanation.surface: A decision about suspending a sentence, right or wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Astray means off course, so gone wrong.

clue.text: Fish in city centre

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for city
a hub is a centre

explanation.surface: A fish swimming in a town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a European freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Light wine counts in Germany

parts.note: to light is to alight, land
Graves is a Bordeaux wine

explanation.surface: A pale wine being tallied up in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective for the wine; it is a verb meaning to come down.
explanation.definitionFit: A landgrave was a German count with territorial rule.

clue.text: Performing animal outside in

indicators.note: outside says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a dog is an animal

explanation.surface: A performing animal kept outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing means carrying out or performing an action.

clue.text: Mount held back by reluctant equestrian

indicators.note: held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A horse held back by a nervous rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' suggests a horse; it is the Sicilian volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a mountain, the volcano on Sicily.

clue.text: Is tame rat breaking bones?

indicators.note: breaking the words up means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Asks whether a pet rat is fracturing bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Metatarsi are the long bones of the foot.

clue.text: Al-Qaeda threat: no time for inaccuracy

indicators.note: no time says T, for time, is removed

parts.note: al-Qaeda's threat is terror

explanation.surface: Sounds like a news report on a terror warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake or inaccuracy.

clue.text: Some of the French in their votes mar constitution

indicators.note: in places the anagram inside the votes

parts.note: the French vote no as non, so their votes are nons

indicators.note: constitution means making up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: French voters spoil a referendum on a constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' points back to the French in the definition: a French voter says non, which is what makes the clue fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Normans were people of Normandy, some of the French.

clue.text: Talk garrulously (rabbit on) in part of France

indicators.note: on places the rabbit after the chatter

parts.note: to gas is to chatter
cony is an old word for rabbit

explanation.surface: Advice to chatter, banging on, somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit on' is British slang for chatter, but here rabbit is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gascony is a historic region in southwest France.
